articles.headline: 8-bit horror Tenebris Somnia mixes weird live-action horror with a retro 2D adventure to impressive and unsettling effect
keyFacts: The upcoming 8-bit horror game Tenebris Somnia combines a retro 2D pixelated adventure with live-action film sequences.
Filmmaker Andrés Borghi produced the high-quality live-action clips, and Airdorf Games serves as executive producer.
The reviewer noted that the slow adventure gameplay can deflate tension, but remains hopeful about the story's depth and imagination.
body: I've been captivated by the idea of wrong-footing an audience ever since playing Faith: The Unholy Trinity. That game presents like an 8-bit horror, then proceeds to bend the rules of what an 8-bit game can do - or perhaps what you remember they could do - in order to surprise and scare you. Tenebris Somnia is very similar. Indeed, it's executive produced by the developer of Faith, Airdorf Games, so the connection runs even deeper. Tenebris Somnia utilises the same retro aesthetic with its grinding chiptune music, its pixelated graphics, and old-school presentation. But the difference is it takes the rule-bending a step further, essentially welding two very different experiences together: a retro-styled 2D adventure and a full-on live-action film. And it's horrific, in all the right ways.

To begin with, Tenebris Somnia is a slow, plodding, fairly unremarkable affair that plays a bit like a point-and-click adventure. You're a young woman on her way to her former boyfriend's apartment, checking it out because you suspect something has happened there. You move from screen to screen, examining points of interest as you pass them, collecting odds and ends - an empty bottle, a mysterious book - and storing them in your inventory for later. Eventually, there's a locked door, and you'll have to piece together the scattered clues in order to unlock it. And despite the apparent urgency of the situation - the carnage you find in your ex-boyfriend's apartment - the pace is slow; deliberately old-school in its approach. Walk back and forth, examine everything, try "combining" items in your inventory, "use" them on the environment. Did it work? No? Try something else.

But this is where Tenebris Somnia begins to distinguish itself: your busywork is often rewarded with a glossy live-action sequence - clips of real actors in impressive costume and make-up enacting key moments from the unfolding adventure. A person with what appears to be two faces, one inverted, rushes out of the darkness toward you. A strange woman suddenly appears in a lift, offering you a gift. Two waxen figures embrace each other in bed. A giant lady with a hole in her face stretches towards the ceiling. It's captivatingly weird and very well-produced, finished with a level of polish that's impressive in an otherwise lo-fi indie experience such as this. And there's a reason for this: the live-action scenes are made by filmmaker Andrés Borghi, who's worked on a number of films including acclaimed Argentinian horror When Evil Lurks. Borghi has also made games of his own, so there's a natural overlap and understanding there.

It's these live-action sequences that stand Tenebris Somnia apart, that bring another, unusual dimension to it. That pixelated creature rushing toward you in the hallway: it has more substance in your mind now you've seen it up close. That enigmatic lady in a cocktail dress: you know the contours of her face and the strange demonic symbols branded there. You know the world better, more intimately now, and that gives it more impact. These live-action moments also create a kind of propulsive anticipation, knowing that when you do solve a puzzle or unlock that mysterious door, lavish reward and revelation awaits you there.

But I have my doubts about the game overall. Granted, I'm only early on, so perhaps I'm yet to really settle in. But I find its plodding stop-start rhythm works against the suspense and horror. Laboriousness deflates the tension. Frequently revisiting areas robs them of their surprises. And I haven't found much inherent interest in exploring new areas of the game; the writing feels functional to me rather than intriguing, and that's a problem, because in the adventure game sequences it has to do so much of the heavy lifting.

But I remain hopeful. I've watched a little more of Tenebris Somnia than I've managed to play, and the movie-making story at its heart - one focusing on a horror short of your ex's creation - appears to deepen and circle back on itself in interesting ways. Everything you do somehow seems tied to that movie - around deals with devilish entities and the grotesque consequences they bring. That filmic motif repeats again and again. And who knows? Perhaps the live-action sequences represent more than the things our character is experiencing. So there's intrigue there, depth, thought, layers, and, by the looks of it, plenty of imagination to support it.

articles.headline: Where to use the coin mining den key in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
keyFacts: Players obtain the coin mining den key in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode by completing the Operation Shopping Hacks mission.
The key unlocks the e-coin mining lab door located in a small apartment block north of The Grid and adorned with a sunglasses advertisement.
Inside the unlocked lab, players can find abundant loot including electronic servers, electronic sensors, and comms modules.
body: The coin mining den key in DMZ in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is one of many keys you can find in the extraction mode, used to unlock a locked door somewhere in the map that contains lots of loot behind it. Obtained by completing the "Operation Shopping Hacks" mission, the coin mining den key is described as opening the "e-coin mining lab in NuriGO West, east of the westernmost gas station inside NuriGO Mall."
That's still somewhat vague, though, so let us direct you to the exact coin mining den key location in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4.
Coin mining den key location in DMZ

The e-coin mining lab is in a small apartment block that can be found directly north of The Grid, specifically on the road north of the Netshin Tech Complex. It's east of the gas station that is on the road leading northwest away from The Grid, and west of the NuriGO Mall stronghold icon on the map. The building itself is adorned with a sunglasses advert on a window on the first floor.

Head inside and climb to the top floor, where you'll find the locked door at the top of the staircase. Use the key to open the door and inside you'll find plenty of loot, including eight electronic servers. If you're on the hunt for electronic sensors, this is the best place to go, and the same goes for if you're in need of comms modules.
We also have guides on where to find high-tenacity fibers, along with where to use the counting room vault key and gun store weapons locker key.

articles.headline: From 2,000 runners to 60,000: The 5-borough New York City Marathon at 50
keyFacts: Fifty years ago, the New York City Marathon expanded to run through all five boroughs for the first time.
About 60,000 runners from over 140 countries are scheduled to compete in Sunday's race.
Organizers adjusted the Mile 20 course route in the Bronx to reduce turns and ease street closures.
body: NEW YORK (AP) — Fifty years ago, the New York City Marathon ran through all five boroughs of the city for the first time.
There were just over 2,000 competitors in that seventh running of the race, including only 88 women. Now about 60,000 runners will step up to the starting line Sunday with nearly half of them women.
Bill Rodgers, a year after winning the Boston Marathon for the first time, won in the debut of the five-borough course and is the only man to win the event four times, from 1976-79.

“I remember everything distinctly, it was so intense,” Rodgers recalled Thursday. “The first time being on the Verrazzano Bridge (at the start), we were nervous. It was so different as we were used to running in Central Park.”

The race was moved out of Central Park in celebration of the U.S. Bicentennial and to help uplift the city, which was struggling. It ended up turning into one of the marquee events in New York and marathoning for the past 50 years.
“The sport really evolved that day,” Rodgers said. “Some ways it's the same, but the competitive side is more and more global then it was during those days.”

There will be runners from more than 140 countries competing Sunday, including defending champion Benson Kipruto of Kenya . He won in thrilling fashion last year, edging Alexander Mutiso by three-hundredths of a second.
Kipruto said he has watched the finish of last year's race many times and each one he marvels at the ending.
“One of my friends ask me, is it real? It looks like a movie and you're the main actor,” Kipruto said. “I was just laughing, so it was really amazing last year.”

Two-time champion Hellen Obiri, who is also Kenyan, returns to defend her title a year after she broke the women's course record in 2 hours, 19 minutes, 51 seconds. That was nearly three minutes faster then the previous best set in 2003 by Margaret Okayo.
“Last year we weren't expecting to run fast," Obiri said. ”First and foremost on Sunday the goal is to win."
The New York City Marathon began in 1970 and the first six years were run inside Central Park doing loops. Obiri said she couldn’t imagine doing that now.
“The fans are great all across New York City and that would be lost,” said Obiri, who ran the race for the first time in 2022 and won it in 2023.
New Yorker Dana Smolin is running the race for the fourth time and agreed with Obiri's thoughts on what makes the race so special.

“There are so many people out there cheering,” she said. “I grew up watching the race and always wanted to run it. I love running through all five boroughs and this year is extra special because it's the 50th anniversary of the five-borough race. Now, when I see kids cheering, I hope I inspire them just like it inspired me.”
Course tweak

For the first time in 15 years there will be a minor change in the course. The runners will take a slightly different route in Mile 20 when the race is in the Bronx. The move was made to reduce the number of turns in the borough from seven to five and will also ease some of the street closures in the area.
New mom
Two-time defending wheelchair champion Susannah Scaroni will look for her third straight title nearly three months after giving birth to her first child.
The fact she's competing left fellow wheelchair racer Tatyana McFadden in awe.

“It's crazy,” said McFadden, who is looking for her sixth New York Marathon title and 25th overall. “I’m excited for her. I think it’s wonderful to see, you know, women, and mothers coming back and racing. We need more support around that and more encouragement.”

articles.headline: The Death Stranding anime's first teaser trailer arrives ahead of its Disney+ debut
keyFacts: Kojima Productions released a teaser trailer for the Death Stranding anime titled Death Stranding Isolations ahead of its streaming debut.
The original story follows a solitary girl whose life changes after encounters with new characters, according to the YouTube synopsis.
The anime is executive produced by Hideo Kojima and directed by Takayuki Sano, and it will premiere on Disney+ next year.
body: The Death Stranding anime's first teaser trailer arrives ahead of its Disney+ debut
The adaptation has a fittingly strange tagline: "My mom became a crater."

Kojima Productions has offered the first proper peek at the Death Stranding anime with a teaser trailer. The brief look at Death Stranding Isolations has a few motifs from the game, such as a courier with cargo strapped to their back. The bulk of the clip focuses on a girl who wakes up in a panic after having nightmares about being consumed by BTs, gloopy entities that are hostile toward living creatures. Dropping this teaser just before Halloween seems quite appropriate, then.

The trailer doesn't shed much light on the story — which is an original tale set in the world of Death Stranding — though the YouTube description offers a synopsis. Death Stranding Isolations takes place right after game protagonist Sam Porter Bridges reconnects North America by way of the Chiral Network. The girl has cut all ties with the outside world and has come to prefer solitude. "Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize," the description reads.

Other characters in the series include "a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning, a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction," and "a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life." The show's tagline is an eyebrow-raiser too — "My mom became a crater," it reads. That's one of the most anime things I've ever heard. It feels deeply fitting for a Hideo Kojima project too.

Kojima — the co-writer, designer and director of both Death Stranding games — is an executive producer on the anime, which is directed by Takayuki Sano. Death Stranding Isolations will hit Disney+ sometime next year.
This is not the only Death Stranding adaptation that's in the works. An animated film dubbed Death Stranding Mosquito is in development, as is a live-action movie that A24 is involved with.

articles.headline: Thunder predicted to trade for 'tremendous' $67.6 million Jalen Williams replacement
keyFacts: Oklahoma City Thunder players Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace sustained serious injuries during a game against the Los Angeles Clippers.
Analyst Eric Pincus proposed that general manager Sam Presti acquire Herb Jones from the New Orleans Pelicans via trade.
The proposed trade would send Jones to the Thunder in exchange for Thomas Sorber, draft picks, and a trade exception.
body: Jalen William's heartbreaking injury in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Clippers puts the Oklahoma City Thunder in an interesting spot.
Williams suffered a dislocated left ankle and a broken fibula, and Cason Wallace tore his labrum in his left shoulder in the same game.
Both players are integral to Oklahoma City's winning DNA. Now, the Thunder will have to adjust.

The Thunder went 39-10 without Williams during the 2025-26 regular season. This time, Bleacher Report's Eric Pincus believes general manager Sam Presti should look to add a player externally via trade.

Pincus' trade proposal has the Thunder acquiring small forward Herb Jones from the New Orleans Pelicans in exchange for Thomas Sorber, a 2027 first-round pick (second-highest of the LA Clippers, top-5 protected Denver Nuggets, and Thunder), a 2027 Chicago Bulls second-round pick, and a $14.9 million trade exception (Herb Jones).
"Herb Jones, via the Lu Dort $17.7 million trade exception, is a tremendous switchable defender, comfortable on the point of attack or covering elite-scoring wings.
"His shooting is inconsistent, but he peaked at 41.8 percent from three-point range in 2023-24. He'd benefit from open looks on a strong squad like the Thunder's," Pincus wrote.
MORE: A former Duke star praises Cam Boozer during preseason
Before Thursday's 16-point, two-steal performance in 32 minutes against the Sacramento Kings, Jones averaged just 3.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals in 17.5 minutes per game.
His role in New Orleans' rotation is clearly not what it used to be, and he could benefit from a change of scenery.
Oklahoma City has multiple first-round picks to offer the Pelicans, something that should be enticing for an organization that has won a combined 47 games in the last two years.

articles.headline: "Trust us when we say it was 'spoiled'": Pentagon probing military freezers full of spoiled food as potential cyberattack
keyFacts: The Pentagon is investigating whether a potential cyberattack caused military base commissary freezers to malfunction and spoil food in August 2026.
Six US military bases reported that their refrigeration units were tampered with overnight to defrost or increase temperatures.
US authorities are collaborating with French counterparts to compare this incident with a similar cyberattack that targeted French supermarkets.
body: - The Pentagon is probing a potential cyberattack on military bases that affected commissary freezers
- Numerous military bases reported malfunctions and issues with refrigeration units in August 2026
- Authorities are in contact with their French counterparts to look for similarities in a similar cyberattack that hit French supermarkets in October
Throughout August 2026, multiple military bases across the US reported issues with freezers malfunctioning and food spoiling in base commissaries.
The Pentagon has now decided to launch an investigation into whether the malfunctions were actually a coordinated cyberattack that echoes a similar recent attack against French supermarkets.

To that end, the Pentagon has confirmed it is in contact with French authorities, and a unit of the US Cyber Command is collaborating with multiple agencies including the Army’s Criminal Investigation Division’s Cyber Field Office.
Freezers set to defrost in midnight attacks

According to Reuters, six military bases reported issues with commissary freezers on social media in August, with Fort Irwin, F.E. Warren, Naval Station Newport, Columbus and Travis all confirmed to have been affected.

The attacks showed similarities to the attack on freezers in French supermarkets, with units set to defrost or temperatures turned up overnight. When commissary workers came in to start work, they found freezers full of hot, spoiled food.
“Trust us when we say it was 'spoiled,'” Fort Huachuca shared on social media.

“We are aware of speculation regarding a potential cyber incident. The Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS), the criminal investigative arm of the DoW Office of Inspector General, is leading a joint investigation,” the Defense Department said in a statement. “For security reasons, we do not comment on ongoing law enforcement investigations.”

The brand that was targeted in the attacks on French supermarkets, Danfoss, said in a statement at the time that many of the supermarkets were running obsolete devices, or devices were running outdated firmware, making it easier for hackers to gain access.

The Internet of Things has made it easier to manage fleets of devices that traditionally would have required individual management - such as freezers and refrigerators in a supermarket - but they also make devices internet facing, creating a potential entry point for hackers.
If the firmware that governs their connectivity isn’t kept up to date, it can become vulnerable to remote takeover, with the hackers able to change settings or hijack the device.

articles.headline: Ex-Wrexham star reveals major obstacle created by Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney
keyFacts: Midfielder Elliot Lee left Wrexham A.F.C. in September as a free agent after mutually agreeing to terminate his contract.
Lee told talkSPORT that the club's celebrity owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, created intense pressure because every opponent treated matches against Wrexham like a cup final.
Lee stated that the owners maintained genuine personal relationships with the players and supported them both on and off the pitch.
body: Having Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney as your football club’s owners has really lived up to the Hollywood billing.

Elliot Lee enjoyed four glorious years with Wrexham A.F.C. from 2022-2026, where he was part of a squad that achieved a historic back-to-back-to-back promotion up the football pyramid, all the way from the National League through to the EFL Championship .
Lee spent four seasons playing for Wrexham, helping them to achieve back-to-back-to-back promotions under Phil Parkinson Getty

Now, the 31-year-old midfielder is currently a free agent after mutually agreeing to terminate his expiring contract with the Welsh club in September, after it became clear that he wasn’t in under-fire manager Phil Parkinson’s future plans.
But the former West Ham United academy product has nothing untoward against the club in any facet whatsoever.
“I absolutely loved my my four years at Wrexham . It was just an incredible experience,” Lee revealed exclusively to talkSPORT during an episode of The S* Word.

“During this off season there was a few talks about, I had a year left on my deal, but I could sort of see myself I wasn’t part of of Phil’s plans going forward. I’m the type of player I just want to be out playing football.

“It was tough to to leave Wrexham and and leave all those memories and people you’ve got to know so well over those years, and everything you’ve been through. But it was a decision I had to make for myself and my own career and it was obviously one Wrexham were happy with as well.”
Lee made 150 appearances across all competitions for The Red Dragons, in which he registered 40 goals and 10 assists – an average of one goal contribution every three games.

Although he misses playing football, the son of former Charlton Athletic , Newcastle United and England midfielder Rob Lee is not rushing to find a new club, even turning down some offers as he continues to process leaving such an “unique and special club” in Wrexham.
Hollywood A-listers created unforeseen obstacle – every game was a cup final
Wrexham became a global soccer phenomenon almost overnight when Hollywood A-Listers Reynolds and McElhenney purchased the club for around $2.67 million (£2 million) back in 2021.
For many teams fighting to move up the football pyramid, Wrexham were suddenly a huge draw for opposing teams, and with that, came added pressure on the club’s players.

“Everyone knew the hype around the club and I think that’s why everyone was so proud to get out of [the] National League, because we’d turn up to places and that team would get their biggest attendance for years, and we had all that to play against,” Lee explained to talkSPORT’s Will Gavin and Kweku Afari.
Parkinson has dragged Wrexham all the way up to the Championship from the National League Getty
Lee was instrumental in the club’s rise from non-league to the second tier of English football Getty

“It wasn’t just as easy as turn up and win. It was a really difficult season in the National League, especially with Notts County there as well. So, I think we’re all really pleased and proud of ourselves for doing that because probably certain people didn’t realize that that would happen every every week, every other week, that it would be teams FA Cup finals playing against us.”
This pressure continued to mount the further Wrexham moved upward, especially when they reached League One following back-to-back promotions.

“Even with with big clubs in League One it was still like, ‘Ah Wrexham, who do they think they are? We’re gonna we want to turn them over there,'” he added. “Every team had a little bit more more motivation to beat us. But I think that’s why it was just an added bonus and had this added reason which made us so proud because of what we did.”
But the pressure didn’t just come from the opposition, it came from the very heart and soul of the club – its own fans and surrounding community.

Lee added, “The pressure was massive at Wrexham, and for me personally as well, and all the lads that are in the changing room, if you haven’t been to like the Wrexham town, everyone lives, eats, breathes football. That is everyone’s life [in] Wrexham.

“And especially with the owners coming in, it got even bigger and bigger. So, it’s like you’re playing to put smiles on people’s faces and to have that pressure of all these people, and then you know it’s gone worldwide as well. …
Wrexham fans have seen their club go from strength-to-strength under their American owners Getty

“But, we we just kept winning and kept winning … And then you realize, ‘We’re in with a with a big shot of doing automatic [promotion] here’. But again, the pressure to create history because we all knew what was at stake. We all knew the back-to-back-to-back had never been done before. …

“But as footballers, you like dealing with the pressure. That’s why you play the game. It wouldn’t be the same if you didn’t have that pressure. It’s just about how you use that pressure to to get the outcomes that you that you work hard for.”
Hollywood owners are really down to earth
At most football clubs, the owners don’t get too heavily involved at the player level, but at Wrexham, there is a real sense of cohesion between ownership, staff, and players.

Of course, Reynolds and McElhenney started documenting the club from the moment they finalized their takeover, showcasing close up the Red Dragons’ ascension up from National League via their television series ‘Welcome to Wrexham’.
With Hollywood actors at the helm, some arguments could be made that they could be presenting themselves in the best light possible for the TV show, and then be completely different off of it.
But Lee reveals that what you see on screen is really what you get, which is something that has surprised a lot of players who have come into the club over recent years.
Lee revealed that what you see is what you get with the owners Getty
McElhenney and Reynolds’ ‘Welcome to Wrexham’ sports documentary series has been a huge hit Getty
“If you speak to any of the lads, especially those from the back-to-back-to-back seasons, they can’t speak highly enough of the owners,” the midfielder said.

“When you’ve been in football a long time as well, you realize it’s not common to have owners like that, to have owners that want to know about, your family, how you are doing here and there, and actually want to help you off the pitch and any problems you’ve got.

“They’ll be there even if they’re across the pond, or wherever they are. They want to help and they weren’t at every match, but if they weren’t at every match, they’d be texting you straight after it. If you score a goal, if you win, they’ll be texting you straight after it. You can guarantee that.

“I think that’s what the lads love. They I don’t think any of us were used to that from an owner before,” Lee continued. “And the way Rob and Ryan came in and just did it differently, they wanted, and they had, a personal relationship with all of us.

“It just made it different for the boys and it made you want to run through a brick wall for them, and that that’s what we did for them. As you see on on Disney, it’s exactly that. We very much had a personal relationship with the owners, and you’d feel like they’d do anything for you.
“We wanted to repay that because we knew how much they done for us, for the club, and even for the town and we wanted to repay that, definitely.”

Although Lee’s – who has also played for Colchester United, Luton Town, and Charlton in his career United – time in north Wales has come to an end, he looks back on his four seasons there as some of the best times in his career.

“It’s been a hell of a journey at Wrexham with so many unbelievable memories,” he lamented. “So many bonds formed and I have such a a huge admiration for the club and everyone around it and I have just such a strong connection with it. I absolutely loved every minute of it.”

articles.headline: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost concerns
keyFacts: US stocks dropped sharply on Friday as investors grew increasingly concerned about the high costs of artificial intelligence investments.
Intel shares fell up to 30 percent after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market and increased AI spending.
Intel finance chief David Zinsner stated that the firm does not expect positive cash flow this year and forecast lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue.
body: - Published
US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.
Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.
The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.
The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.
On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect positive cash flow this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

articles.headline: Trump will rally in Iowa and Kansas after initial cancellations
keyFacts: President Donald Trump will hold rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday after initially canceling them, a source told the Washington Examiner.
Trump and Vice President JD Vance are campaigning to boost GOP turnout and help Republicans maintain control of Congress.
The Republican National Committee announced that Trump will also host 19 tele-rallies in the final weekend before Election Day.
body: President Donald Trump will hold rallies in Iowa and Kansas over the last weekend before the midterm elections after the events were canceled just one day earlier, a source familiar with the matter confirmed to the Washington Examiner .
“The rallies are back on,” the source said. “President Trump loves his supporters, and in addition to nearly 20 tele-rallies, he will hold back-to-back rallies in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday.”

On Thursday, Trump campaigned in South Carolina to boost Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) in her race against Democrat Annie Andrews while news spread that the Iowa and Kansas rallies were scrapped in favor of nearly two dozen tele-rallies.

While returning to Washington, Trump told the Washington Examiner that he was confident in Sen. Roger Marshall’s (R-KS) race against Democrat Adam Hamilton and that he no longer needed to travel to the Sunflower State.
“I think he’s doing well,” Trump said. “We’re going to do a tele-rally for him instead. He’s doing very well, actually.”

Hamilton leads Marshall by 2.6 percentage points, according to a RealClearPolitics poll average . The Cook Political Report rates the race as a toss-up, despite Trump winning the state in 2024 by more than 16 points over then-Vice President Kamala Harris.
The Republican National Committee also announced Thursday that Trump would hold 19 tele-rallies in the final weekend before Election Day.
“Voters across the country want to hear from President Trump before Election Day, and this 72-hour sprint will be a huge boost in the closing days,” RNC Chairman Joe Gruters said in a statement.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance have relentlessly traveled the nation to boost GOP turnout in traditional red-leaning states and help save the Senate from flipping to Democratic control. Election forecasters are predicting Democrats will flip control of the House.

The president is set to travel to Florida, where he will campaign for Rep. Byron Donalds (R-FL), who is running for governor, and other GOP candidates. Vance scrapped his plans to travel to Minnesota to hold a press conference on Friday. The vice president will also go to Rome, New York, on Monday to stump for Anthony Constantino, a bombastic candidate who finds himself in a competitive race despite running in a deep-red seat.
But sources said Trump remains dedicated to helping his fellow party members retain control of both chambers of Congress and remains the best party messenger for the GOP.

“No one works harder, fights harder, or loves the American people more than President Donald J. Trump,” said the source who confirmed the rallies are back on. “The rallies were rearranged for scheduling purposes to accommodate dozens of additional tele-rallies that were recently added to the president’s schedule.”
TRUMP AND VANCE OFFER GLIMPSE OF MAGA’S FUTURE ON MIDTERM CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Trump will hold tele-rallies in these states: Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, and Virginia.
More states could be added.

articles.headline: Japan’s Gundam Is Gone, But It’s Getting Two Life-Sized Monster Hunter Statues
keyFacts: Capcom announced plans to build life-sized statues of Rathalos and Lagiacrus in Fukuoka, Japan.
The statues will face each other in the center of a new park located in the Marinoa Resort area.
Capcom stated that the statues are intended to serve as a gathering place and a pilgrimage point for fans.
body: Japan is home to numerous attractions that bring fictional worlds to life. Across the nation, numerous life-sized Gundam have recreated the famous massive humanoid robots (though one of these titans in Tokyo was recently taken down after nearly two decades of service). You can even visit Dragon Quest Island, an entire theme park designed to make you feel like you’ve stepped into the world of the games. Most of these examples, however, have only been willed into existence by almost half a century of loyal support. Capcom, meanwhile, is capitalizing on a more recent cultural phenomenon, announcing that it will soon be erecting life-size statues of two of the most iconic Monster Hunter creatures.

Monster Hunter has been a phenomenon for the company since the PS2 days, though for many years this success was mostly localized to domestic Japanese fans. It was Monster Hunter Worlds that really transformed this domestic hit into a global phenomenon. Nowadays the franchise is bigger than ever with both local fans and inbound tourists. Perhaps because of this, the company has announced plans to build life-sized representations of Rathalos and Lagiacrus in Fukuoka, a major city on the southern island of Japan. The statues will stand in the center point of an all-new park being built in Marinoa Resort, set against the coastal waters to the north of the city, as part of a revitalization project in the area. Based on initial promotional photos shared with the announcement, the statues will face one another, as if in conflict.

In recent years, the company has sought numerous ways to translate the success of its biggest hit into various real-world events. Last year, it operated a limited-time AR-powered attraction called Monster Hunter Bridge inside World Expo 2025. Capcom has also regularly run limited events for the franchise in partnership with Universal Studios Japan as part of its Cool Japan event partnering with various popular domestic IPs. Now, with the company also planning to make Monster Hunter Bridge a permanent attraction at Nijigen No Mori theme park in Hyogo Prefecture, it hopes this statue spot will serve as a point of pilgrimage and a gathering place for hardcore fans of the series.

Between the two attractionsâMonster Hunter Bridge and the statuesâit may even be possible to plan an entire holiday around visiting these commemorations of Monster Hunter. With Japanese tourism increasingly relying on popular IP as a method of attracting visitors to locations beyond the typical hotspots, perhaps these new Rathalos and Lagiacrus statues can pave the way to transforming Fukuoka into a new location for tourists to come to during their travels.

articles.headline: New York fights over a rent freeze. Minneapolis has results
keyFacts: Landlords and New York City Hall are fighting in a Manhattan courtroom over text messages and the approval process for the recent rent freeze.
A study found that Minneapolis home values were 15% to 20% lower over the first five years following its 2020 zoning changes.
Minneapolis apartment construction grew through the 2040 Plan, while smaller triplex builds remained low and housing prices and rents dropped compared to similar cities.
body: Weeks into New York’ s rent freeze, the argument over it has moved to a Manhattan courtroom, where landlords and City Hall are fighting over text messages and whether the mayor leaned on the board that voted it through.

The court will decide whether the freeze was approved properly. What no court can change is what a freeze does: It protects the tenants who already have a lease and adds not one home for the people who don’t. For them, the useful evidence is 1,000 miles west, in Minneapolis, six years into the country’s most closely watched zoning experiment.

In January 2020, Minneapolis became the first large U.S. city to rid of single-family zoning. About 70% of its residential land allowed one house per lot. The 2040 Plan allowed three, let bigger apartment buildings rise along the main corridors, and a year later dropped parking minimums. None of it forced anyone to build. The city just stopped saying no.

Both sides said what they expected, which means we can check. Mayor Jacob Frey , making the pitch in May 2018, noted that anyone could already knock down a modest ranch house and put up a mansion, and said the plan merely let the same lot hold “something more affordable.” Minneapolis for Everyone, the residents’ group that organized against the plan, predicted it would “make our city less affordable.”

Six years is enough time to find out who was right. In a new study with two colleagues, we followed Zillow’s home values for every Minneapolis neighborhood from 2013 through 2024 and compared them with three yardsticks: The 50 cities most similar to Minneapolis, the big cities of the Midwest, and, since the plan’s first year was also the year of the George Floyd protests, the cities that had large protests of their own. Pick whichever yardstick you like, the answer barely moves.

Over the plan’s first five years, a typical mid-priced Minneapolis home was worth, on average, something like 15% to 20% less than it would have been without it. The effect was larger for the cheapest third of homes, which grew every year instead of wearing off, and it spilled into the nearest suburbs. Zillow puts a typical Minneapolis home at around $330,000 today. Our estimates say the house would have run $60,000 to $80,000 more had the plan never passed, roughly what a 20% down payment would’ve cost.

To be clear, prices in Minneapolis did not drop. They rose about 15% from 2019 to 2024, while the typical U.S. city saw them rise by roughly half. Homeowners kept the equity they had. What they didn’t get was the run-up most of the country got.

How, when hardly anyone built a triplex? The Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis counted last week: About 300 homes in two- to four-unit buildings since 2020, around 2% of the apartment units the city permitted in those years. The homes came instead as apartments of the kind the same plan made easier to build: Nearly 21,000 homes permitted from 2017 to 2022, most in buildings of 20 units or more, enough to grow the city’s housing stock by 12%. Our own permit data are less clear on the total than on the shape: Fewer buildings, each holding about a third more homes. And since buyers shop across the city line, the suburbs next door, Edina and St. Louis Park, saw prices held down too.

To be sure, 2020 was a strange year in Minneapolis, and the same Fed team argued last year that the city’s slow rent growth has more to do with a Minneapolis-specific drop in demand that year than with new supply. We tested the two obvious sources of such a shock. Had people been fleeing the unrest, the price damage should have shown up first around George Floyd Square; it didn’t. Population growth did slow by about a percentage point per year, not enough on its own to move prices this far. Weaker demand probably explains a slice of the gap; it is hard to see how it accounts for most of it.

Building has slowed in Minneapolis since 2022, as it has nearly everywhere, with borrowing and construction costs where they are, and the Fed’s new report spends most of its pages on that. It also finds that Minneapolis rents have fallen nearly 20% after inflation since 2020, about twice the drop in comparable cities. Most of the lead the city built in the plan’s first years is still there.
ABDUL EL SAYED’S MEDICARE FOR ALL NEEDS A BLACK BOX WARNING

For other cities, three things in the record stand out. The price response came fast, about 5% in the plan’s first year, and grew from there. It did not hinge on the plan’s most famous provision; the triplexes were a footnote, and the apartments the plan also allowed did the work. And none of it stopped at the city line.

Most of what sets the price of a house is beyond any city’s reach: Interest rates, lumber, wages , and how many people want to move there. The rulebook for what may be built is not, and Minneapolis is the first big city to have loosened it and then waited long enough to see what happened. It spent nothing. It built nothing itself. The result fits on one line of a mortgage application: $60,000 to $80,000 that the next family buying there will not have to borrow.
Vitor Melo is a Regulatory Policy Fellow at the Archbridge Institute. He holds a PhD in economics from Clemson University and completed postdoctoral work at the University of Chicago.

articles.headline: Pope Leo calls for the disarmament of AI: ‘Machines are tools, not persons’
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV called for the disarmament of artificial intelligence during a Friday address.
Pope Leo encouraged United Nations member states to ban lethal autonomous weapons at a Geneva meeting next month.
Pope Leo stated that human oversight must remain mandatory for decisions affecting human life and the use of force.
body: Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be “disarmed,” adding that humans “have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications.” In Friday’s Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to “take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons” during their meeting in Geneva next month.
Pope Leo calls for the disarmament of AI: ‘Machines are tools, not persons’
UN member states should take steps to ban ‘lethal autonomous weapons,’ Pope Leo says.

The address reflects many of the ideas Pope Leo laid out in his first major papal document in May, which highlighted “safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence.” In line with his encyclical, Pope Leo tells participants that “Machines are tools, not persons,” and warns about the dangers of granting AI systems rights or legal personhood. “Decisions affecting human life, freedom, and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed, and responsible human oversight,” Pope Leo says.

In 2024, Pope Francis similarly called for a ban on autonomous weapons, saying, “No machine should ever choose to take the life of a human being.” AI has become a popular topic for Pope Leo, who suggests he chose his name because he must confront advances in the technology — similar to how Pope Leo XIII presided over the church at the forefront of the Industrial Revolution.

Pope Leo closes out his address by calling for international institutions to safeguard the common good from AI-related risks, along with “shared standards, independent oversight and clear mechanisms of accountability so that decisions concerning the development and use of AI can be examined, challenged when necessary, and accompanied by appropriate remedies for any harm caused.”

articles.headline: Forest Green launch legal proceedings against Savage departure, England win controversial U-15 World Cup match, and more – football live
keyFacts: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca clarified that goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma is droppable like any other player, despite currently being first choice.
Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi stated that James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace following an injury scare.
Forest Green owner Dale Vince said the club started legal proceedings to sue Peterborough and former manager Robbie Savage for £2m.
body: Maresca clarifies that Donnarumma is not un-droppable
Enzo Maresca has clarified that Gianluigi Donnarumma is droppable like any other Manchester City player, having said following Wednesday’s Carabao Cup win over Brighton that it is “Giogo plus 10”.

Donnarumma’s form is currently uneven, with City’s No 1 at fault for Aston Villa’s winner in last Saturday’s 2-1 defeat. The Italian also made errors for two goals in the 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.
In reference to the City manager’s comment about his team being Donnarumma and 10 others, Maresca was asked if there are any other undroppable players.

“I think one thing is to say that in this moment it is Gigio is plus 10 and another thing to say [he is] un-droppable,” the City manager said. “Yes, there are two different things. There is no player that is un-droppable. But at this moment it is Gigio plus ten.”

Maresca also brushed off Fabian Hurzeler’s comments after the Carabao Cup tie, where the Brighton head coach stated City had the “luck” and that Saturday’s league meeting between the sides at the Etihad Stadium is about “revenge”.

Maresca said: “This is what he said. Every manager can say something different. It depends on what you see with your eyes. But I respect what he said. “We’re going to try to do our best and try to win the game. If it’s revenge or these kinds of things, it’s more about them, not about us.”
Apart from Antoine Semenyo, who has a knee injury, Maresca has all of his squad available.
Spurs get Maddison injury boost ahead of Palace clash
James Maddison will be available for Tottenham when they take on Crystal Palace despite an injury scare after he limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs’ 2-0 victory at Chelsea.

After Maddison had endured a slow start to the campaign with caution preached over his fitness following a May return from anterior cruciate ligament damage, his substitution last Saturday looked to be another setback.

But, ahead of the Palace game, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: “James is available. This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.
“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.
“So, I think it’s not a problem if he loses two days (training), but then we have to analyse if we take risk or not.
“If we take risk like Pedro Porro (against Aston Villa) or (Dejan) Kulusevski. We are lucky to have a big squad and it’s important to not take risk with new injuries.” Press Association
Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt will be in the Fenerbahce dugout when his old club visit Istanbul in the Champions League next week after the Turkish club named him as interim manager.

Kuyt, 46, took over from Ismail Kartal, who resigned following Monday’s 2-1 derby defeat by Galatasaray and Fenerbahce’s baord have now confirmed the Dutchman will remain in charge until the next international break.
“The committee established by our board will carry out the work to appoint our new head coach, and the process will be accelerated,” Fenerbahce said in a statement.
The former Netherlands international spent six seasons at Liverpool between 2006 and 2012 before joining Fenerbahce, where he won the Turkish league title in 2014.
‘Where we want to be’: Le Bris stays positive as faltering Sunderland face Coventry reunion

Twenty seconds of stoppage time remained when Enzo Le Fée picked up the ball and kissed it before taking a corner. As intended, the Frenchman’s perfect, right-footed delivery dropped into the corridor of uncertainty that leaves goalkeepers torn between leaving their line or standing firm.

It also dipped at the right moment for Dan Ballard to power a header in off the crossbar. Extra time in the 2025 Championship playoff semi-final second leg was almost over and Sunderland had secured a 1-1 draw that consigned Coventry to a 3-2 aggregate defeat.

As an outpouring of the loudest, most raucous emotion imaginable left the Stadium of Light feeling as if it was literally shaking, Régis Le Bris momentarily looked bewildered. By the time joyous comprehension began spreading across the Sunderland manager’s face, Frank Lampard was already a study in misery. Sunderland were on their way to Wembley, leaving Coventry in the Championship for another year.
Read Louise Taylor preview of Sunderland’s meeting with Coventry in full:
Hello, me again. Shall I kick-off with some Super Franky Lampard? Here he is discussing this weekend’s bottom-of-the-table clash between Coventry and Sunderland.
Asked whether Saturday’s result could be key for both sides, the Sky Blues manager replied:
No, it’s too early for that. It’s a good opponent who are a very strong team.
They are a strong team and in Europe, been in this league now for a couple of years. It is very early to talk about where they are and where we are.
To find the consistency is what top teams manage to do. Some of our players in terms of Premier League experience are learning in real time. We have to learn quickly, improve quickly.
We’ve all been given another challenge and they have to relish it and take it head on.
Maresca on 'aggressive' Brighton and City's right direction
Round two of Man City v Brighton at the Etihad after their midweek Carabao Cup game there went all the way to penalties.

“They are doing very good, on and off the ball, they are very aggressive, man-to-man oriented, they attack very good with so many players. It’s going to be a tough game,” City manager Enzo Maresca said in a press conference, adding that they score many goals against teams. No Premier League side has more than Brighton (23) this season.

Asked whether there is no more established Premier League Big Six, he replied: “You can have one or two surprises every season but now the level is so similar, you can drop points against any team and win against any team. It’s more of a similar level.
It’s very good for the Premier League, that’s why so many people probably love the Premier League because you never know.”

Four months have passed since Maresca’s appointment. Unsurprisingly, he is happy with how his table-toppers are faring. “I think we go in the right direction. I said in the last press conference, after changing manager and many players after so many years, it takes time to compete again – and we are competing in all competitions.”

It appears that the Bolivian goalkeeper chose not to try and save England’s decisive penalty in protest at what he saw as an inaccurate call by the referee. Bolivia felt the foul which led to the spot kick had occurred outside the box.

After England then loudly celebrated their goal, Bolivian players then ran over to the ref to berate him. While they were held back by coaching staff from both countries, one player was ultimately shown the red card.
FIFA are awaiting the officials’ report on the game. This was, remarkably, the 936th game of the tournament, and England’s last, after they finished in Tier B of the competition.
The Tier A final will be contested later today by Czechia and Spain.
The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) charity has said it is “deeply saddened” after items were stolen from a memorial to the Munich air disaster in the German city.

The memorial display in Manchesterplatz honours the 23 victims of the disaster, which occurred when the plane transporting Manchester United home from a European Cup tie in Belgrade crashed after refuelling in Munich on February 6, 1958.
The tragedy took the lives of eight United players.
The MMMF said it was notified earlier this week that the memorial display case had been vandalised and that items had been taken.
They said United had offered to pay for repairs but that it had already agreed to cover the costs.
MMMF chair Ifty Ahmed said: “The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft.

“Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich air disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world.

“Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember. Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable.” Press Association
Forest Green launch legal proceedings against former manager Savage's departure
Forest Green owner Dale Vince says the club have started legal proceedings over their former manager Robbie Savage’s departure to Peterborough.
Vince told Sky Sports News: “We are suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for £2m, which was the buyout clause that we were cheated out of. And that process began last week.”
Vince claimed there was “an abundance of evidence of an approach” made by Peterborough’s chair, Darragh MacAnthony.

Peterborough declined to comment on the latest development, but Posh chairman Darragh MacAnthony has previously posted on X that the appointment of Savage was “100 per cent proper, following all rules”.
Savage left National League side Forest Green four weeks ago.

Under-21 football should be scrapped. There are 18-year-olds retained only so clubs have a big enough squad to support the one player who could become a diamond. A boy should be released at latest 18. Those who stay should be in the first team or on loan.
Young players need the competitiveness of senior football as soon as possible. Academy football is tidy and highly technical but has little resemblance to the frenetic, physical senior game.

It also doesn’t test whether a boy has the mentality to cope in a tough dressing room where older players don’t want you taking their place. As a young player at Nottingham Forest I dribbled in training past an older teammate who warned: “Do that again, son, and I’ll break your leg.” It’s not like that any more but you need a certain character.
After two Premier League wins on the trot, Fulham took a back-step on Wednesday with a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Carabao Cup, despite controlling play and dominating possession.

“I think we can do better in the final third,” manager Álvaro Arbeloa said in his press conference this morning. “We controlled the game, we had the possession but even with that, we could have created more chances. It’s something we need to improve. We need to work on it and do better in the final pass and be more clinical in the finishing.”
He said that front men Gonzalo García and Rodrigo Muniz needed better service. In a clash of Spanish managers, his side face Unai Emery’s Aston Villa tomorrow evening.
“We are in a process as a team; in every process, there are ups and downs. I think we need to learn from our mistakes,” he said.

He also said that Emile Smith-Rowe, a peripheral player this season, needed to be patient for his chance. “Emile is a very talented player, like others,” he said. “They need to keep working as they are doing and they need to wait for their opportunity.”
Brighton hope to have Chema Andres and Ferdi Kadioglu available for their second trip to Manchester City of the week.
Andres and Kadioglu sat out Wednesday’s Carabao Cup tie at the Etihad Stadium after suffering hip injuries at Liverpool on Saturday.
But both are expected to return for the Premier League visit this weekend, when Charalampos Kostoulas will also be available after he was rested in midweek.
However, Pascal Struijk will not be available when Brighton look for revenge after being knocked out of the cup on penalties.
Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said at a press conference in Manchester on Thursday: “A positive was that (Yankuba) Minteh and Mats Wieffer had their comeback yesterday.
“Ferdi, Chema, also Kostoulas (who) we rested yesterday, we are quite convinced that he will be an option for Saturday.” PA
Michael Carrick: United players have 'hunger to do better'
Should he stay or should he already have gone? It doesn’t get any easier for under-fire Michael Carrick as his side face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in tomorrow’s early kick-off.
Following their 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Manchester United are 16th in the Premier League and on their worst run without a victory in all competitions since 2015.

“The boys, I have to say, are hungry,” Carrick said in a press conference today. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games, but there’s an intensity, there’s a bit of an edge, there’s a disappointment, there’s a hunger to do better, for sure.”
Surely this match is Carrick’s last chance. He appears to be ignoring all the noise. “My responsibility is the players,” he said. “The outside is not anything for me to focus on.

“I know what we can affect, I know what we need to improve. I know as a group, leading a group, what help they need a little bit as well and a bit of guidance at certain times and dealing with certain things.”
Carrick also confirmed that Bruno Fernandes retains the club captaincy and is “fully committed” to the cause.
Everton manager David Moyes’ news conference is due to start in a few minutes’ time, we’ll bring you the news from that. I’m sure the dropped Jack Grealish will come up again…

They were on song last night at home in the Carabao Cup last night against Newcastle, with Jordan Pickford showing his pedigree in the first-half before goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry. They will play Fleetwood in the quarter-final.
But first, more of the same: they are away to Newcastle on Monday night.

985 not out…yes, that shy and not retiring (yet) Portuguese mega-star is nearing the magical mark.

He scored a 15-minute hat-trick to help Al-Nassr to a 5-3 win over Al Kholood yesterday. His club are second in the Saudi Pro League behind Al Qadsiah on goal difference. Never mind his 30-day suspension for walking out on a Portugal training camp – at this rate, the 41-year-old could hit four figures in early 2027.
News to wound hipster football fans: Inter and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the San Siro from the 2031-32 season.
It will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost £1bn.
Say it ain’t so. Looks nice, but it’s not got the beauty or dignity of the spiral walkways, has it?

That means no wonder boy in the squad when they play Liverpool on Sunday, as well as their next games against Hull and Newcastle. More drama involving England. They beat Bolivia 3-2, with the goalkeeper standing passively by the goalpost and making no effort to save the match-winning spot kick.
According to the PA, Bolivia players then appeared to confront the referee, as well as England players, before both sides finally left the pitch in Azerbaijan, which is hosting the tournament.

This comes four days after the abandonment of their match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. The matter has been referred to a FIFA independent disciplinary committee.
The Premier League’s bottom two teams play on Saturday, as Sunderland travel to Coventry.

Wearsiders will have fond memories of Dan Ballard’s late winner in the 2024-25 Championship play-off semi-final against Frank Lampard’s side. No chance of a similar intervention this time round, with the centre-back absent due to a thigh issue. Romain Mundle is also out, with knee problems.
With two wins in their last three matches, Coventry are on the up and “competitive”, according to Régis Le Bris, who spoke in his press conference about what changes with promotion to the top tier:
“Now you don’t have the same amount of possession so it’s a new balance and you have to learn.
“It’s always a new story. Coming from last year to this season, we had the World Cup, a few injuries and a tough start in the Premier League with a busy schedule.
“It means they have to adapt and to learn with this new I won’t say overload, but this new journey and schedule and it takes time.”
In case you missed it last night: Everton left Jack Grealish out of their squad for yesterday’s 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United following a “breach of club discipline”.

It is understood the 31-year-old missed training on Monday without permission and the decision to drop him was taken by manager David Moyes in conjunction with the club’s chief executive Angus Kinnear.

Everton paid £12m in total to have Grealish on loan last season and are paying a similar sum for this campaign. He will become a free agent at the end of this season when his lucrative contract with City expires.
The 'nervous system changes' behind Kulusevski’s comeback

Dejan Kulusevski returned to competitive action for Tottenham after a 17-month injury layoff to play the last few minutes in the club’s 3-1 home victory against Coventry last week and followed that up with another substitute appearance in Saturday’s win at Chelsea.
Kulusevski had multiple setbacks after knee surgery in May 2025. But a second procedure in March finally set him on the road to recovery.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s match against Crystal Palace, the 26-year-old Kulusveski told SpursPlay: “It had been like one year and a couple of months and I still can’t walk on the stairs. I can’t walk on the stairs like a normal guy. I have to play football so in my head I’m not going to give up, but I have to think that if this doesn’t work out, what do I do?

“I went to a physio in Sweden. He was able to change my nervous system and then it felt different. When I did the exercises, I said, ’I don’t have pain, like this hurt yesterday. Why is this not hurting today?’

He added: “There was still pain but it was different. Now I had control of my leg and then that is when the grind started that summer. I started to play football and it got better every day. I was limping and everything, but it was different now.
“I got much stronger in a short time and I went from ’this guy will not play football any more’ to playing really good football in just a couple of weeks.” AFP
Thanks Tom. From the Premier League to South Korea, experiencing an autumn of discontent after their poor World Cup showing.
Coach Hong Myung-bo and KFA president Chung Mong-gyu resigned, were questioned by parliamentarians and then police raided KFA offices.

This divided team’s leading man is Son Heung-min, but even his place is not guaranteed, as John Duerden explores. The discussion around the ex-Spurs veteran could move to whether he should start at all, which was previously borderline unthinkable.
Bruno Fernandes owes Manchester United a performance, Mathys Tel has arrived at Spurs and Liverpool are improving… here are your ten things to look out for this weekend in the Premier League:
Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
Tom Garry
Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament.

Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s “ambition” was to have “equality” for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.” There had, therefore, been widespread hope across the women’s game that 2027’s prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis.

Marco Rose will hold Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi back for a little longer despite more minutes in midweek. A foot injury sidelined Kroupi for the first three months of the campaign, but the highly rated French attacker returned in the 3-0 win over Manchester United and was introduced in the 80th minute of Wednesday’s Carabao Cup triumph over Aston Villa.

Ahead of Saturday’s visit of Leeds, Rose told a press conference: “We still need to build up his game time. I’m really happy to have him back, to have his quality, but he knows that he has to be patient in this situation to not get in a difficult situation with another injury.
“We need to get him fit, in a good spot with more and more match time in between good sessions of training.”
The Cherries remain without Alex Scott, but he could return from a thigh injury next week.
Brighton hope to have key duo back for round two with City

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler said he is confident that Chema Andres and Ferdi Kadioglu will be available as Brighton seek immediate revenge on Manchester City after being knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the Etihad Stadium on penalties in midweek.

Andres and Kadioglu suffered hip injuries at Liverpool last weekend, but both are expected to return at the Etihad after sitting out the cup tie, while Charalampos Kostoulas will also be available after he was rested on Wednesday night.
However, summer signing Pascal Struijk will not be available, he is out with an undisclosed knock.
Hurzeler told media in Manchester on Thursday: “A positive was that (Yankuba) Minteh and Mats Wieffer had their comeback yesterday.
“Ferdi, Chema, also Kostoulas (who) we rested yesterday, we are quite convinced that he will be an option for Saturday. This is the new information we can give.
“Regarding Pascal Struijk, he won’t be an option for the weekend, but we are quite convinced that he will be back afterwards.” Press Association
U-turn on Afcon as tournament reverts to two-year cycle
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will revert to being held every two years after the continent’s ruling body reversed its decision taken last year to move to a four-year cycle.
The African Football Confederation (Caf) said in a statement that it had: “Unanimously decided that the CAF Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to taking place every two years.”

Caf said part of the reasoning for performing a U-turn on the decision was the length of time it would take for Afcon’s replacement competition, the Africa Nations League Pan-African Competition, to become financially viable.

“We were also concerned by the several years required before the proposed new Africa Nations League Pan-African competition, (which was supposed to be identical to the current Afcon and take place every two years), could make the substantial financial and football development contributions for African Football and Caf competitions to be globally competitive and self-supporting,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in the statement.

Motsepe added that the decision was also taken in the interests “of African players employed by football clubs outside Africa”. That may prove contentious with their clubs looking at losing key players every two years as opposed to four.
Next year’s tournament is being co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda and CAF said the following three would take place in 2028, 2031 and 2033.

“The forthcoming Fifa World Cup will take place in 2030 and in accordance with the Fida tradition, the final tournament of the Afcon and other confederations national team competitions may not take place during the year of the Fifa World Cup,” said Motsepe, explaining the three-year gap between the 2028 edition and the scheduled 2031 tournament.
